title: WOMEN'S BASKETBALL | Sam Purcell Media Session - 11/24/26
text: I know, at this point last year, you were talking a lot about playing a complete game for all four quarters uh after starting six and zero and heading into you know a tough stretch over the next few. How what do you feel like is the thing this team needs to work on the most or is the thing that could you know kind of bite them in these games that they don't work on it? >> Yeah, yeah, great question. Um I'm I'm not so much playing four complete quarters. I might change that after the next five games. Um cuz again each team's different, each players are different. Um I have so much confidence in this team. I love again I start with my point guard play. I've never had two point guards um like this. I've always had great at least one, but to have two um is really special. It's almost like my first year. I thought I had two good point you know two good point guards, but this one these these two are really really special. Um so again I just I'm just trying to instill confidence. We got to every day, every situation so new, making sure they understand what they want out of me, but making sure I set them up for success. And then what I'm trying to see instead of so much four quarters is play with joy. Um I talk about how these young ladies are winners. I couldn't be more happy with their character and who they are and how hard they work, but when we come together on the court, don't play perfect. Basketball's a game of mistakes and that's where I've been really excited what you saw in the Southern Miss game. Do we have areas that we need to get better in? You better believe it, but the connected energy that this group has is fun to watch. They cover for each other like I've never seen and one example in the Southern Miss game that you saw was the charges they took that were huge. Their willingness to sacrifice their body and then you got someone like Madison Francis who is one block away from 100 blocks. We're not even at the end of her sophomore year and then you got Favor Wadozi who's one of the top rebounders in the country. Again just is they're a joy to coach because they just find a way and that's what I want to keep doing. Just find a way and when the moment happens when it does we'll figure it out. >> Do you do you have an update on Grace after she didn't play Sunday? >> Yeah, so Grace hopefully be returning >> to practice today and definitely was really excited about where she was at. She's been under the weather, so we just didn't take her to Southern Miss and it's that time of year of Thanksgiving holidays and Thanksgiving weather changes, so unfortunately she got the bad end of the straw. >> And then how big is Macy Pfeifer's versatility been for you guys being able to play multiple positions? >> Yeah, Macy Pfeifer Macy Pfeifer. I can say Macy Pfeifer all day and I appreciate you asking that question cuz she is three through five. She can play everything. Um I can play her at the wing when Cali went down. I can play her, you know, backup minutes for Madi and then if we have to we'll play her in the post. She doesn't care. She just has a nose for the ball, blue collar mindset and coach I got whatever you need and again I can't say enough things about her. She's a glue piece and I was excited to see uh the moment some of the big moments come for her. That uh drive that Reese had that um she got a paint touch and kicked out to Macy Pfeifer was a dagger three in that second half and that young lady deserves it cuz she works so hard. >> Uh you've talked about wanting to schedule some road games early and you've got through that stretch and you're still undefeated. Uh what do you think that does for this team's confidence moving forward? >> Yeah, hopefully a lot. Um again you know the three values that we're really hanging our hat on this year for our team is toughness, um discipline and you know being connected and so road trips allow that opportunity as for to break bread. Uh we challenge them to sit different seats and make sure we get to truly know each other, but then just get in on on a hostile environment somewhere away from the hump and and figure out what we got to do together um to find a way to win and so we've had two close scrimmages that we've been on the road and then obviously Buffalo was a hard trip, UT Martin was a long trip and then obviously going down to Southern Miss, you know hopefully we'll have some carryover for the way we play coming next week cuz boy are we going to need it uh to make sure we come out the gate against Indiana. >> Yeah, on Sunday it was kind of uh a showcase of you know the sport in Mississippi whether it was Jayda on the other team playing against Tudé, high school teammate Macy having her best game and as how would you characterize the health of the sport in this state and from where, you know, maybe it was a few years ago when you first became aware? >> Yeah, really good question. Uh, it's really strong right now, really strong, which is exciting. Um, if you look at the amount of players that are coming out of here to your point, um, it's at an all-time high and that's just not me being emotional about it. It's factual based on if you look at the high school rankings where they have these kids. You've got several top 100 kids over the next three years that are from here where those last four years that I've been here on the job, you maybe had one or two at max. Um, and then then it's the kids like Tootie who haven't been ranked at all that, you know, haven't been evaluated that if you really do your work that you know that there's some hidden gems here and they're just prideful if they're given the opportunity like we did with Tootie to put give her a jersey that she'll show everybody in the country what you missed out on. And so when you topple that with an in-state rival cuz that game means a lot for those young women, Macy, Tootie, um, especially. I mean they were fired up for the opportunity to your point to play some other kids within the state, but most importantly represent this university with a lot of pride in that game. >> I'm sure on what you've seen with TCU, but just tell me what are your thoughts on the Indiana and TCU heading in this week? >> Yeah, so uh, I'll start with TCU first. Obviously Mark Campbell has done a phenomenal job. I mean you think about when they came here my second year when we played them in the WNIT and where he's been able to take that program since. Um, he's got them in the lead eight every year. The financial support that they have provided at TCU is phenomenal and he's been able to go get some of the top transfer portal uh, players in the country not only for those reasons, but also the way he coaches. He's a great coach. He's got a great style. The the kids that they go after, they believe in it and that's why they've been able to put a product on the floor that's been one of the top eight pro, you know, programs in the country over the last three years. And then back to Indiana, um, again I can't say enough about Terry Moren. Uh, the young, you know, the lady's a winner. Um, she she's won at Indiana. Obviously they had an off year last year, and she's hungry. They've got a young lady, Maliah Samuels, uh that our fan base should be uh familiar with. She was at USC, uh Southern Cal. And um we played her in the NCAA tournament, and she was one if you go back in my press conference that I talked about where I never uh did a scouting report where I put three point guards on there. Uh but Maliah Samuels was that kid. And now she's left Southern Cal and went to Indiana in a starting role. She's just a glue kid, a difference maker, a water bug. I could go days for days. The young lady's special, and then she's got special players to go around it. So uh when you put a great coach, a great point guard with great post play and great shooters, this should be for one heck of a matchup that we've got again have great practices. Uh and we need to be dialed in if we're going to try to find a way to win this first round. >> All right, thanks. >> Good. Thanks everybody. Appreciate y'all. >> Happy Thanksgiving.
